statement: For a root canonical CNF F measured by the current C025 input_size_units N = max(2, 1 + m + L + n), one complete ordinary Resolution elimination of one variable, charged before optional subsumption and with duplicate resolvents charged at most once in the implementation, cannot exceed N^2 state units. Therefore a RAW root context cannot be an explicit-elimination over-cap witness when cap_exponent = 2.

definitions.m: number of clauses in the current root CNF
definitions.L: total literal occurrences in the current root CNF
definitions.n: number of variables in the current root CNF
definitions.p: number of clauses containing pivot x

proof.step_1: There are at most p*q <= m^2 pivot pairs. Tautological pairs only reduce output.
proof.step_2: Ignoring deduplication and subsumption can only increase the upper bound, so it is safe to charge every pair as if it produced a distinct resolvent.
proof.step_3: For a positive parent P and negative parent Q, the resolvent contributes at most one clause-count unit plus |P|+|Q|-2 literal units, hence no more than 1+|P|+|Q| units.
proof.step_4: Summing pair contributions gives at most p*q + q*sum_{P}|P| + p*sum_{Q}|Q| <= m^2 + 2mL.
proof.step_5: Retained clauses contribute at most m+L units; adding the global leading unit yields U' <= 1 + m + L + m^2 + 2mL.

implementation_is_no_worse_than_bound: duplicate resolvents are stored in a set
canonical subsumption after raw generation can only shrink the returned CNF

consequences.where_a_C2_barrier_can_first_appear: A later elimination from an intermediate state measured against the original root N^2 cap, because the intermediate state may already have grown relative to root input size.
consequences.next_search_focus: Reachable intermediate states after one or more exact transitions; test the next exact elimination against the unchanged root N^2 cap.

forbidden_overinterpretation: Do not claim that all elimination sequences stay within N^2.
Do not replace the root-relative cap with a cap recomputed from each intermediate state.
